subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should skill lifecycle management live in core Skill Workshop, a plugin/ClawHub extension API, or be deferred until a narrower lifecycle API is designed?
rationale: The remaining work would create durable proposals from run outcomes, rank or hide skills from usage data, and add new config/storage surfaces; automation cannot choose that policy boundary safely.

options.title: Design extension seam first
options.body: Define the minimum core/plugin API for skill usage, outcome signals, and reviewable lifecycle actions before implementing auto-repair or retirement policy.

options.title: Implement in core Skill Workshop
options.body: Treat skill optimization and retirement as first-party core behavior, accepting the added config and persisted state after a maintainer-owned design.

options.title: Defer or decline
options.body: Leave Skill Workshop focused on explicit user corrections and manual proposal review until stronger demand or a safer plugin model exists.

recommendation.title: Design extension seam first
recommendation.body: Define the minimum core/plugin API for skill usage, outcome signals, and reviewable lifecycle actions before implementing auto-repair or retirement policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter owns the latest current-main shape of the affected Skill Research and config files and is the strongest routing candidate for the product-boundary decision.
